hero.title: MacBook Cleaner for macOS
hero.lead: Storage cleanup and performance monitoring for your Mac — processed locally.
hero.started: Your download has started — {{fileName}}. When it finishes, follow the steps below.
hero.quickStepsUnnotarizedLast: Launch the app — the first time, use Open Anyway.

requirements.title: Will it run on my Mac?
requirements.intelNote: Intel Macs aren’t supported by this verified build.

steps.title: Download the DMG
steps.body: Click Download for Mac. The disk image is saved to your Downloads folder.

steps.title: Open the DMG
steps.body: Double-click {{fileName}} in Downloads. A window opens showing the app and your Applications folder.

steps.title: Drag to Applications
steps.body: Drag MacBook Cleaner onto the Applications folder, then eject the disk image from Finder’s sidebar.

steps.title: Launch the app
steps.body: Open MacBook Cleaner from Applications or Launchpad. Run it from Applications — scheduled cleanup only works from there.

gatekeeper.title: Seeing a security warning?
gatekeeper.intro: That’s expected right now — here’s why, and how to open the app safely.
gatekeeper.noticeTitle: MacBook Cleaner isn’t notarized by Apple yet
gatekeeper.noticeBody1: Apps distributed outside the Mac App Store are normally signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized. This version is signed ad hoc — without a Developer ID — and isn’t notarized, so the first time you open it, macOS Gatekeeper says it can’t verify the developer or check the app for malicious software. This message doesn’t mean a problem was found — it means Apple hasn’t reviewed this build.
gatekeeper.noticeBody2: Only download MacBook Cleaner from this website. If you got the file anywhere else, delete it.
gatekeeper.howtoTitle: Open it once via System Settings
steps: Open MacBook Cleaner from Applications. When the warning appears, click Done (or Cancel) — don’t move it to the Trash.
Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and scroll down to the Security section.
Next to the message about MacBook Cleaner being blocked, click Open Anyway, then confirm with your password or Touch ID.
Click Open in the final dialog. macOS remembers your choice, so you only need to do this once per version.
gatekeeper.tip: On macOS 14 Sonoma and earlier you can also Control-click the app in Applications, choose Open, then click Open again.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.body: macOS may ask to let the app access Downloads, Desktop and Documents, and to control Finder when you first clean. Full Disk Access is optional.

updates.title: Updates
updates.body: Settings → Check for Updates checks, downloads, and verifies new versions for you — nothing installs without your confirmation, and you'll need to restart the app once to finish. Your settings are kept.

uninstalling.title: Uninstalling
uninstalling.body: Turn off Scheduled Cleanup and Launch at Login, then drag the app to the Trash.
